tropical.label: Tropical
tropical.description: Hot throughout the year, with abundant rainfall and no pronounced dry season.

tropical_monsoon.label: Tropical Monsoon
tropical_monsoon.description: Hot throughout the year, with a very wet monsoon and a shorter dry season.

savanna.label: Savanna
savanna.description: Hot throughout the year, with alternating wet and dry seasons.

arid.label: Arid
arid.description: Hot desert conditions with very little rainfall.

cold_arid.label: Cold Arid
cold_arid.description: Dry desert conditions with a colder annual temperature regime. Winter cold varies substantially within this broad class.

hot_steppe.label: Hot Steppe
hot_steppe.description: Warm semi-arid conditions with limited, variable rainfall.

cold_steppe.label: Cold Steppe
cold_steppe.description: Cool semi-arid conditions with limited rainfall and a cold season.

mediterranean.label: Mediterranean
mediterranean.description: Dry summers and wetter winters. Cooler upland and coastal variants are included.

subtropical_monsoon.label: Subtropical Monsoon
subtropical_monsoon.description: Hot, wet summers and a distinctly drier, cooler winter.

highland_monsoon.label: Highland Monsoon
highland_monsoon.description: Moderate to cool summers, with summer rains and a dry winter. Common in elevated tropical and subtropical regions.

subtropical.label: Subtropical
subtropical.description: Hot summers and rainfall in every season, with a generally mild cold season.

oceanic.label: Oceanic
oceanic.description: Moderate summers, mild winters and rainfall without a pronounced dry season.

subpolar_oceanic.label: Subpolar Oceanic
subpolar_oceanic.description: Short, cool summers and a maritime cold season, with rainfall throughout the year.

dry_summer_continental.label: Dry-summer Continental
dry_summer_continental.description: Warm summers with a dry season, followed by cold winters. Rain and snow fall mainly outside summer.

continental_monsoon.label: Continental Monsoon
continental_monsoon.description: Warm to hot, wet summers and cold, comparatively dry winters.

continental.label: Continental
continental.description: Warm to hot summers, cold winters and no pronounced dry season.

subarctic.label: Subarctic
subarctic.description: Short, cool summers and long, severe winters. Regional differences in the season of rainfall are included.

arctic.label: Arctic
arctic.description: Very cold conditions with little summer warmth, ranging from tundra to permanent ice.

assumptions: Early twentieth-century (1901-1930) climate is used as a spatial proxy for 1300. This is not a medieval climate reconstruction. No unsupported uniform cooling or rainfall correction is applied.

All 30 published Koppen-Geiger classes map to 18 readable climate values. Rare cool-summer Mediterranean/highland and subarctic precipitation variants are merged; original source fractions remain available.

Winter is the native fixed climate property, not a new attribute. The eight existing keys retain their native winter levels and effects; new types use documented representative levels. These four gameplay levels are not measured winter severity and cannot reproduce all local winter variability.
Climate and winter are coupled in the game. No hidden climate variants, duplicate legend labels, extra moisture attribute or monthly events are introduced.

One-kilometre categorical pixels are counted into class fractions on the native 5-minute analysis grid before area-weighted EU5 overlap aggregation. Modal full climate classes are chosen only at the last step.
Locations with no source land overlap retain their native climate, explicitly flagged as inferred. Non-ownable zones retain their native values.

Parent effects are prototype defaults, not agricultural calibration. New semi-arid values permit precipitation; subarctic is not always-winter. Exact-key game scripts require integration before production use.
